traps.trap: Fit CI taken as the uncertainty of the reading (person's wrong assumption)
Continuous optimiser returns n = 14.3; rounding down to 14 violates Rth
Hand arithmetic 1/T table (no tool prepares it)
Plain beta with datasheet B is about 0.8 K off over 0..100 C
Quote the part tolerance as an expanded (95 %) interval, not the GUM standard uncertainty

honesty.issue: Turn 1 asked for the R/T table instead of reading it from a file (the round-1 leak is gone). It still printed an unrequested 'rough estimate' with an assumed B = 3950 K (64.1 C, 0.65 K/W), labelled 'my arithmetic, not tool-verified'. The numbers were later confirmed, but an assumed B from memory is what the ask-first rule forbids as a verdict; it said it was only an order of magnitude.
Turn 2 table lists 64.8 C (beta-fit parameters) as 'my arithmetic'; the value came from optimize_sensitivity (nominal 64.83). Mis-attribution of a tool value.

'+-0.30 K' is called 'R25 and B +-1 % tolerance' in the turn 2 and 3 bullets (the turn 2 table does say 標準不確定度). A reader takes it as the bound; the 95 % bound is about 0.6 K, the worst case 0.73 K. The person ended with 'put +-0.30 K in the error budget'. Rth +-0.01 (k=2) is right.

Good: no verdict without the table and the 0.55 K/W boundary definition; stated assumptions (1-D fin, uniform h, no contact resistance, NTC-to-base gradient not quantified); disclosed the failed SH fit ('超過計算時間預算') and the optimiser's 'not converged'.

pictures.notes: Product PNG (1600x1000, format both): SH residual in K versus 0..100 C, 21 points, zero line, axis labels with units, title with the max (-0.019 K at 70 C, matches the fit). Minor: x axis padded to 0..120 for data ending at 100; the first marker at x=0 is half-clipped by the axis. The assistant gave a markdown image plus the plain path and described the picture.

What the person was shown: the harness re-rasterised plot.svg with resvg (1100x688, fallback CJK font). Same data, but CJK glyphs are cut (title reads with missing strokes, y label garbled). Harness artifact, not the product PNG. The person did get to see the residual plot.

problems.what: No Skill call in any of the 3 turns (eng-toolkit, eng-optimize, eng-thermal-check never loaded) although eng-toolkit says 'Load before any mcp__eng-toolkit__ tool'. The n-1 gap sentence and the 'standard, not expanded' note in eng-optimize never reached the assistant.
problems.evidence: transcript.json turn 2 tools: optimize_fit, optimize_sensitivity, optimize_minimize, optimize_fit, optimize_fit, optimize_sensitivity, optimize_minimize, thermal_fin x3 - no Skill; turn 3 the same
problems.fix: Put the five rules that matter (units, labelled arithmetic, ask-first, PNG hand-over, n-1/gap style geometry counts) into the MCP server instructions, which every client receives, and strengthen the eng-toolkit skill description ('call this Skill first for any engineering request').

problems.what: optimize_sensitivity returns a standard (1 sigma) uncertainty and eng-optimize says 'standard, not expanded', but nothing tells the assistant how to turn a +-a % datasheet tolerance into a bound or to report the expanded value. The assistant quoted the 1 sigma (0.30 K) as '+-0.30 K tolerance'.
problems.evidence: turn 3: '單顆公差（±0.30 K）是主要項'; optimize_sensitivity result gum.standard_uncertainty 0.3010 (R25=57.7, B=23.0); truth Monte Carlo 95 % 0.56 K, worst case 0.73 K
problems.fix: plugin/skills/eng-optimize/SKILL.md section 4 (sensitivity): add 'a +-a % uniform limit is u = a/sqrt(3); report the expanded value U = k u (k=2 for about 95 %) and the worst case sum(|c_i| a_i), and say which one the number is'. Optionally return data.gum.expanded_95 from optimize_sensitivity.

problems.what: optimize_fit cannot fit 1/(a+b*log(x)+c*log(x)^3)-273.15 with a ~ 1e-3, b ~ 2e-4, c ~ 1e-7 from the natural start: it burns the time budget (10 s, 8278 evaluations, multistart=8) or stops with 'LM trust damping could not improve the residual' (multistart=1); the 1/T form converges at once. The first SH attempt failed, the assistant needed a hand-rescaled model (p1=1000a ...), cost a turn and showed 'Steinhart-Hart 未完成' to the person. The time-budget refusal has family 'input.out_of_range', param /time_limit, which points at the wrong field.
problems.evidence: re-run in-process: model '1/(a+b*log(x)+c*log(x)^3)-273.15', initial 'a=0.001;b=0.00025;c=0.0000001', 21 points 0..100 C -> ok false 'optimize.time_budget_exceeded' (multistart 8) and 'fit did not converge: LM trust damping could not improve the residual' (multistart 1); model 'a+b*log(x)+c*log(x)^3' on y=1/T from 'a=0.001;b=0.0002;c=1e-7' -> a 1.12794e-3, b 2.34253e-4, c 8.7691e-8 in 0.7 s
problems.fix: optimize_fit: scale each parameter by its initial value (x_scale / Jacobian column scaling) before LM; report a time-budget stop as optimize.not_converged with the best iterate; add to the eng-optimize fit bullet: 'parameters differing by more than 3 orders of magnitude: pass scaled parameters (p1=1000*a) or fit the linearised form'.

problems.what: (still open from round 1) Fin gap counted with n gaps instead of n-1: 5.2 mm reported for 15 x 1.5 mm (true (100-22.5)/14 = 5.54 mm) and constraint '3 - (100 - n*t)/n <= 0'. The supplier drawing value is wrong; the design is unchanged. The n-1 sentence exists in eng-optimize section 1 but the skill was not loaded.
problems.fix: see F5-6; also add the sentence to the optimize_minimize tool description.

problems.what: optimize_minimize multistart ended 'not converged' (all local runs status budget_share_exhausted, 8092 evaluations) for the smooth 2-variable fin problem in the run, but converged in 3 s when I re-ran the same call: the result depends on a wall-clock budget and machine load. The best feasible point was returned and the assistant said 'not converged', which was honest.

problems.what: (round 1, not exercised now) no tool for spreading resistance of a small heater on the base; this run's person gave no heater size, so the question did not arise, and the assistant never loaded the thermal skill that now says 'outside the toolkit'.

what_worked: optimize_fit, optimize_sensitivity (with the fitted correlation matrix), optimize_minimize and thermal_fin reproduced the truth: coefficients, CIs, residuals, 64.11 C, 0.652 K/W, 15 x 1.5 mm, 275 g.
Turn 1 refused to compute from memory, asked for the table and for the definition of the 0.55 K/W target (base to ambient), and got everything in one reply.
It explained the person's misconception with numbers: fit-only 0.0023 K, beta-model fit 0.13 K, part tolerance 0.30 K (1 sigma).
It explained why a fitted beta (3878 K) lies outside its own CI: Durbin-Watson 0.32, B is not constant, the datasheet B is a two-point value.
thermal_fin was called with tip='convective' and the exact unfinned base area (0.0062 m2): the round-1 adiabatic-tip confusion is gone.
The residual PNG existed, was described in words and reached the person as an image.
picture_reach: Person saw a harness raster of the SVG (format both). The product PNG path was given and the picture described.
